phases.account: Maintenance environment: Configurator app default user 'edgeuser'. After the OS is installed: the local administrator credentials given when provisioning (simplified provisioning) or the non-built-in local admin you create, with the same credentials on every node. Do not use the built-in Administrator.
phases.available: Bootstrap logs exist once the Azure Stack HCI OS is installed and bootstrap/Arc registration starts. Arc agent and extension logs exist from Arc agent install onward. Before the OS is installed, the maintenance environment keeps its logs under /var/log; get them through the Configurator app support package.
phases.access: WinRM to the node IP (NTLM): add the node to the workstation's TrustedHosts or use HTTPS 5986, and always pass -Credential. A non-built-in local admin may also need LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=1 on the node (not stated for Azure Local). Alternatives: the Configurator app support package, or RDP (Learn's route for the bootstrap logs).

phases.account: Maintenance environment: Configurator app default user 'edgeuser'. After the OS is installed: the local administrator, with the same credentials on every node. If the nodes were joined to the domain before deployment (2604 or later), the deployment (LCM) user must be added to local Administrators.
phases.available: Bootstrap logs exist once the Azure Stack HCI OS is installed and bootstrap/Arc registration starts. Arc agent and extension logs exist from Arc agent install onward.
phases.access: Nodes are normally still in a workgroup at this point, so use WinRM by IP with TrustedHosts (or HTTPS 5986) and -Credential. Use Kerberos by host name only if the nodes were joined to the domain beforehand.

phases.account: The built-in Administrator (the account the OEM image or the OS setup gives you) until the deployment local admin exists; after that the deployment local admin (non-built-in, same credentials on every node). The built-in Administrator is renamed ASBuiltInAdmin when deployment starts, so switch accounts before Validate/Deploy.
phases.available: From the moment Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization runs on the node. Arc registration does three things: (1) when the OEM image is not the latest for its release baseline, the OS image update (zero-day solution update: Scan, Download, Install; typically 40-45 minutes, then a reboot, after which Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization is run again; meanwhile the registration status shows Update: InProgress); (2) the bootstrap (NetworkConfig, RemoteConfig, WebProxy, TimeServer, HostName, then ArcConfiguration: ArtifactsUpload, ConnectivityValidation, ArcRegistration, ArcExtensionInstall); (3) the Arc machine (named after the host) appears in the resource group and its agent turns Connected. Logs: setup.log, arcInstallLog-*.txt and AzStackHci.ArcConnection.Debug.log\PowerShell_transcript.* under Bootstrap\Logs; himds.log and azcmagent.log under AzureConnectedMachineAgent\Log once the Connected Machine agent is installed. The mandatory extensions are not part of this phase: they install during cluster Validate.
commands: Get-ArcBootstrapStatus (on the node; $s = Get-ArcBootstrapStatus; $s.Response.Status: Succeeded, or Failed: rerun the registration with a new ARM token or device code)
Get-ArcZeroDaySolutionUpdateStatus (on the node; the OS image update: Scan, Download, Install)
Collect-ArcBootstrapSupportLogs (on the node, when a failure persists: collects the logs to share)
phases.access: WinRM to the node IP (NTLM): add the node to the workstation's TrustedHosts or use HTTPS 5986, and always pass -Credential. A non-built-in local admin may also need LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=1 on the node. RDP or the console also work at this stage.
phases.observed: Seen live 10 Oct 2026 on a 2609 Local Identity node (read later, during Deploy, as the deployment local admin): C:\Windows\System32\Bootstrap\Logs holds setup.log, arcInstallLog-*.txt and AzStackHci.ArcConnection.Debug.log\PowerShell_transcript.*. Not yet checked during an Arc registration itself or with the built-in Administrator. Read live 11 Oct 2026 on an OEM-image node (module AzureEdgeBootstrap 1.0.0): the cmdlet names Get-ArcBootstrapStatus and Get-ArcZeroDaySolutionUpdateStatus, their { Version, Response } shape and the step names (Update: Scan, Download, Install; Bootstrap: NetworkConfig, RemoteConfig, WebProxy, TimeServer, HostName, ArcConfiguration with ArtifactsUpload, ConnectivityValidation, ArcRegistration, ArcExtensionInstall). Status values other than NotStarted, the Errors[] entry shape and Collect-ArcBootstrapSupportLogs are from Learn only.

phases.account: The deployment local admin (localAdminUserName): non-built-in, with the same credentials on every node. Learn documents no separate LCM user for Local Identity.
phases.available: Environment Checker output is written to C:\CloudDeployment\Logs when validation runs as part of deployment, and each run overwrites the file. Standalone checker runs write to $HOME\.AzStackHci instead. Learn documents C:\MASLogs\LcmEceLiteLogs for upgrade validation only; for deployment it is unverified. The mandatory Arc extensions (AzureEdgeDeviceManagement, AzureEdgeLifecycleManager, AzureEdgeRemoteSupport, AzureEdgeTelemetryAndDiagnostics) install during Validate; their logs are under C:\ProgramData\GuestConfig\extension_logs on each node.
phases.access: WinRM to the seed node by IP: TrustedHosts or HTTPS 5986, -Credential, and an account in local Administrators. CredSSP is not needed.
phases.timing: Learn (ARM template flow, 12.2609 latest): Validate mode takes about 10 minutes (the portal wizard and the rack aware template say about 15 minutes for one or two machines, longer for bigger deployments). Do not select Try again while validation tasks are running.

phases.account: The local administrator (the same on every node). Learn does not say whether the deployment (LCM) user is a local admin during validation, unless the nodes were joined to the domain before deployment and it was added to Administrators.

phases.account: The deployment local admin (localAdminUserName), with the same credentials on every node.
phases.available: During and after cloud deployment on the seed node (watch progress from the seed machine). Learn does not name the deployment log files or describe how they rotate. The limited and full Environment Checker runs happen first.
phases.access: WinRM to the seed node by IP: TrustedHosts or HTTPS 5986, -Credential, and an account in local Administrators. Fallbacks (both are Azure writes, so opt-in only): Arc run command (preview, output capped at 4 KB, needs runCommands/write) or Arc SSH (needs Owner or Contributor and sshd running on the node).
phases.observed: Seen live 10 Oct 2026 on a Local Identity Deploy pass: logs written to C:\CloudContent\MASLogs, C:\MASLogs and C:\Observability; C:\CloudDeployment\Logs did not exist yet ~10 min in.
phases.timing: Learn (12.2609 latest): once Deploy mode starts, a limited Environment Checker run and then a full Environment Checker run happen first, then cloud deployment starts; after a few minutes you can watch it in the portal. The whole deployment takes 2.5 to 3 hours and several steps take 40-50 minutes or more. Begin cloud deployment takes 45-60 minutes. The longest step is Deploy Moc and ARB Stack: 40-45 minutes. Azure can lag behind the node: the step list may say Deploy not started while the seed node is already working (Sonar labels that).

phases.account: The local administrator. During cloud deployment the LCM (deployment) user is added to local Administrators on the nodes, and the nodes are joined to the domain.
phases.available: During and after cloud deployment on the seed node. Learn does not name the deployment log files or describe how they rotate.
phases.access: Use WinRM by IP with TrustedHosts (or HTTPS 5986) and -Credential until the domain join completes. After that, Kerberos by host name with the LCM user works without TrustedHosts.

phases.account: The deployment local admin, which you maintain yourself. RecoveryAdmin, whose password is stored in the cluster Key Vault. The built-in Administrator is renamed ASBuiltInAdmin. Nodes stay in a workgroup (ADAware = 2).
phases.available: The logs stay on the nodes after deployment. On-demand collection (Send-DiagnosticData or the portal's Send logs) works once the AzureEdgeTelemetryAndDiagnostics extension is installed, and needs the Azure Stack HCI Administrator role. For deployment failures, use standalone collection with Send-AzStackHciDiagnosticData.
phases.access: WinRM by IP with TrustedHosts (or HTTPS 5986) and -Credential. RDP is turned off after deployment. Learn lists Arc SSH (sshd enabled on each node) as the remote route for Local Identity clusters.

phases.account: The LCM (deployment) user, which is in local Administrators. The local administrator; if that is the built-in account, it is renamed ASBuiltInAdmin. AD users or groups only if they are added to local Administrators (for example by a GPO that nests a domain group).
phases.available: The logs stay on the nodes after deployment. On-demand collection (Send-DiagnosticData or the portal's Send logs) needs the AzureEdgeTelemetryAndDiagnostics extension and the Azure Stack HCI Administrator role.
phases.access: WinRM with Kerberos by host name and a domain account (no TrustedHosts needed). Connecting by IP falls back to NTLM and needs TrustedHosts or HTTPS. RDP is turned off after deployment.

phases.account: The deployment local admin: the non-built-in local administrator with the same credentials on every node (Learn names this account for cluster management operations such as adding or repairing a node; it names no separate update account). Reading the logs needs an account in local Administrators on the node.
phases.available: During a solution update the orchestrator (Lifecycle Manager) runs an update action plan: Sonar follows it from the Azure update run (clusters/updates/updateRuns: steps, start and end times, errors) and shows the node log of the seed node as it is written. Learn names no update log files. A failed update can be resumed in the portal (Resume an update) or watched on a node with Start-MonitoringActionplanInstanceToComplete -ActionPlanInstanceID <id>. Cluster-Aware Updating runs inside the update; if CAU attempts fail, investigate the first failure by its start and end time with Get-CauReport.
phases.timing: Learn does not give one duration for a solution update: each step may carry an expected execution time (Sonar shows it when Azure reports it). A node reboots during the run; the Arc agent and the logs are unreachable meanwhile.
commands: Start-MonitoringActionplanInstanceToComplete -ActionPlanInstanceID <id> (on a node, as the deployment user)
phases.access: WinRM to the seed node by IP (TrustedHosts or HTTPS 5986, -Credential) or, once the nodes are domain-joined, Kerberos by host name. Sonar only reads.
phases.observed: Built from Microsoft Learn and the REST reference only: unverified against a live run.

phases.account: Run on an existing node: Add-Server with the new node local administrator credentials; on Local Identity deployments the cluster management account is the deployment local admin (non-built-in, same credentials on every node), which you keep up. Reading the logs: an account in local Administrators on the nodes.
phases.available: From Add-Server (PowerShell) or Add machine (portal, preview). Since release 2508 a validation runs first and returns details when a test fails. Learn names no add node log files. Monitor with Start-MonitoringActionplanInstanceToComplete and the operation id that Add-Server returns; after it ends the storage pool rebalances in the background (low priority, can take days: Get-VirtualDisk | Get-StorageJob returns nothing when done). The new node can take several hours to show in the portal (Sync-AzureStackHCI speeds it up). Rerun a failed operation with Add-Server -Rerun.
phases.timing: Validation, then the add node action plan, then a storage rebalance that can run for multiple days (Learn).
phases.access: WinRM to the existing seed node by IP or by host name (domain-joined: Kerberos). The incoming node is still in a workgroup until it is added; use TrustedHosts or HTTPS 5986 and -Credential for it.
phases.observed: Built from Microsoft Learn and the REST reference only: unverified against a live run. Azure does not publish an update-run style resource for this operation in the REST reference; set track to add-node in the config and Sonar shows the Arc machine and the node log.

phases.account: Run on an existing node as the domain user from deployment (AzureStackLCMUser or equivalent) with the new node local administrator credentials. Reading the logs: an account in local Administrators on the nodes.

phases.account: Run on another member node: Repair-Server with the repaired node local administrator credentials (by default the built-in Administrator); the cluster management account is the deployment local admin (non-built-in, same credentials on every node). The node name must be the NetBIOS name.
phases.available: From Repair-Server. Before it, reimage the node, register it with Arc with the same parameters as the others and give it the Azure Stack HCI Device Management role and Key Vault Secrets User. Since release 2508 a validation runs first. The operating system, drivers and firmware are updated as part of the repair. Monitor with Start-MonitoringActionplanInstanceToComplete; storage rebalances on the reimaged node afterwards (can take days). Rerun a failed operation with Repair-Server -Rerun. Learn names no repair log files.
phases.timing: Validation, the repair action plan, then a storage rebalance that can run for multiple days (Learn).
phases.access: WinRM to a member node by host name (Kerberos) or by IP with TrustedHosts or HTTPS 5986 and -Credential. The node being repaired is reachable by IP only until it has rejoined.
phases.observed: Built from Microsoft Learn and the REST reference only: unverified against a live run. Set track to repair in the config and Sonar shows the Arc machine and the node log.

phases.account: Run on another member node as the domain user from deployment (AzureStackLCMUser or equivalent) with the repaired node local administrator credentials (by default the built-in Administrator). The node name must be the NetBIOS name.
